Argentina.name: Aconcagua
Argentina.note: Highest peak in the Americas and outside Asia (6,961 m), in the Andes.

Argentina.name: Ojos del Salado
Argentina.note: Highest active volcano in the world (~6,893 m), on the Argentina–Chile border.

Chile.name: Ojos del Salado
Chile.note: Highest active volcano in the world (~6,893 m), on the Argentina–Chile border.

Chile.name: Villarrica
Chile.note: One of Chile's most active volcanoes, in the Lake District.

Ecuador.name: Chimborazo
Ecuador.note: Farthest point from Earth's centre due to equatorial bulge, despite not being the tallest peak.

Ecuador.name: Cotopaxi
Ecuador.note: One of the world's highest active volcanoes (~5,897 m).

Peru.name: Huascarán
Peru.note: Highest peak in Peru (~6,768 m), in the Cordillera Blanca.

Colombia.name: Nevado del Ruiz
Colombia.note: 1985 eruption triggered a lahar that buried Armero, killing over 20,000.

United States.name: Mount Whitney
United States.note: Highest peak in the contiguous US (4,421 m); Denali in Alaska is higher still but sits outside this map's frame.

United States.name: Mount Rainier
United States.note: Most glaciated peak in the contiguous US; a lahar risk for nearby Tacoma/Seattle.

Mexico.name: Pico de Orizaba
Mexico.note: Highest peak in Mexico (~5,636 m) and third-highest in North America.

Mexico.name: Popocatépetl
Mexico.note: Active volcano near Mexico City and Puebla; frequent ash-plume eruptions.

Canada.name: Mount Logan
Canada.note: Canada's highest peak (5,959 m), in the Saint Elias Mountains, Yukon.

Ethiopia.name: Simien Mountains
Ethiopia.note: Rugged UNESCO-listed massif, home to endemic gelada monkeys.

Kenya.name: Mount Kenya
Kenya.note: Africa's second-highest peak (5,199 m), an extinct volcano straddling the equator.

DR Congo.name: Mount Nyiragongo
DR Congo.note: Active volcano with one of the world's largest persistent lava lakes.

Morocco.name: Jbel Toubkal
Morocco.note: Highest peak in North Africa (4,167 m), in the Atlas Mountains.

France.name: Mont Blanc
France.note: Highest peak in the Alps (4,808 m), on the France–Italy border.

Italy.name: Mount Vesuvius
Italy.note: Buried Pompeii in 79 CE; still active and looms over Naples.

Italy.name: Mount Etna
Italy.note: Europe's most active volcano, on Sicily.

Russia (European).name: Mount Elbrus
Russia (European).note: Highest peak in Europe (5,642 m), in the Caucasus — a dormant volcano.

Nepal.name: Mount Everest
Nepal.note: Highest peak on Earth (8,849 m), on the Nepal–China border.

Japan.name: Mount Fuji
Japan.note: Japan's highest peak and an active (dormant) volcano, sacred in Shinto and Buddhist tradition.

Indonesia.name: Krakatoa
Indonesia.note: 1883 eruption was heard thousands of km away and caused a global temperature dip.

Indonesia.name: Mount Tambora
Indonesia.note: 1815 eruption — the most powerful in recorded history, caused the 'Year Without a Summer'.

Philippines.name: Mount Pinatubo
Philippines.note: 1991 eruption was the second-largest of the 20th century, cooling global temperatures briefly.

New Zealand.name: Mount Cook / Aoraki
New Zealand.note: Highest peak in New Zealand (3,724 m), in the Southern Alps.

New Zealand.name: Mount Ruapehu
New Zealand.note: North Island's highest peak; an active volcano within a ski-field.

Papua New Guinea.name: Mount Wilhelm
Papua New Guinea.note: Highest peak in Papua New Guinea (4,509 m).
